**Charlize Theron** ([/ʃ ɑːr ˈ l iː z ˈ θ ɛr ə n/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_shar-LEEZ THERR-ən_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-pron2-1)Afrikaans:[[ʃarˈlis ˈtrɔn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Afrikaans "Help:IPA/Afrikaans");[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-pron1-2) born 7 August 1975) is a South African[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Nationality-3) and American actress and producer. One of the world's highest-paid actresses,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-forbes19-4)[her accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_Charlize_Theron "List of accolades received by Charlize Theron") include an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") and a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award"), in addition to nominations for three [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs") and two [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards").

Theron came to international prominence in the 1990s by playing the leading lady in the [Hollywood films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States")_[The Devil's Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Advocate\_(1997\_film) "The Devil's Advocate (1997 film)")_ (1997), _[Mighty Joe Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mighty\_Joe\_Young\_(1998\_film) "Mighty Joe Young (1998 film)")_ (1998), and _[The Cider House Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cider\_House\_Rules "The Cider House Rules")_ (1999). She received critical acclaim for her portrayal of serial killer [Aileen Wuornos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aileen_Wuornos "Aileen Wuornos") in _[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_(2003\_film) "Monster (2003 film)")_ (2003), for which she won the [Silver Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Bear_for_Best_Actress "Silver Bear for Best Actress") and [Academy Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress"), becoming [the first South African to win an acting Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Best_Actress "List of African Academy Award winners and nominees"). She was nominated twice more for the Oscar for portraying a sexually abused woman seeking justice in the drama _[North Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_Country\_(film) "North Country (film)")_ (2005) and [Megyn Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megyn_Kelly "Megyn Kelly") in the biographical drama _[Bombshell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombshell\_(2019\_film) "Bombshell (2019 film)")_ (2019). She received praise for playing troubled women in [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman")'s comedy-dramas _[Young Adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Adult\_(film) "Young Adult (film)")_ (2011) and _[Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tully\_(2018\_film) "Tully (2018 film)")_ (2018).

Theron has starred in several commercially successful action films, including _[The Italian Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Italian\_Job\_(2003\_film) "The Italian Job (2003 film)")_ (2003), _[Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock\_(film) "Hancock (film)")_ (2008), _[Prometheus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prometheus\_(2012\_film) "Prometheus (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[Mad Max: Fury Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Max:\_Fury\_Road "Mad Max: Fury Road")_ (2015), _[Atomic Blonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic\_Blonde "Atomic Blonde")_ (2017), and _[The Old Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Old\_Guard\_(2020\_film) "The Old Guard (2020 film)")_ (2020), as well as several _[Fast & Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_&\_Furious "Fast & Furious")_ installments: _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ (2017), _[F9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F9\_(film) "F9 (film)")_ (2021), and _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_X "Fast X")_ (2023). On television, she earned a nomination for the [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actress_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie") for her portrayal of [Britt Ekland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britt_Ekland "Britt Ekland") in the biographical film _[The Life and Death of Peter Sellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Life\_and\_Death\_of\_Peter\_Sellers "The Life and Death of Peter Sellers")_ (2004).

Since the early 2000s, Theron has ventured into film production with her company [Denver and Delilah Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_and_Delilah_Productions "Denver and Delilah Productions"). She has produced numerous films, many in which she had a starring role, including _[The Burning Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Burning\_Plain "The Burning Plain")_ (2008), _[Dark Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark\_Places\_(2015\_film) "Dark Places (2015 film)")_ (2015), and _[Long Shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Shot\_(2019\_film) "Long Shot (2019 film)")_ (2019). Theron became an American citizen in 2007, while retaining her South African citizenship. In 2016, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ named her one of the [100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").

## Early life

Charlize Theron was born in South Africa, in [Benoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng "Benoni, Gauteng") in [Transvaal Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transvaal_Province "Transvaal Province") ([Gauteng Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng_Province "Gauteng Province") since 1994).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-5) She is the only child of [road builders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_construction "Road construction")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) Gerda ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9e "Née") Maritz)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):16-18 and Charles Theron.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):16-18, 34 Her great-granduncle was [Second Boer War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Boer_War "Second Boer War") military leader [Daniel Theron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Theron "Daniel Theron").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):14 She is from an [Afrikaner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaner "Afrikaner") family, and her ancestry includes Dutch as well as French and German. Her French forebears were early [Huguenots in South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huguenots_in_South_Africa "Huguenots in South Africa").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):14 Although Theron is fluent in English, her [first language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_language "First language") is [Afrikaans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaans "Afrikaans").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-9) She grew up on her parents' farm in Benoni, near [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-WIRED-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-13)

When Theron was 15, on 21 June 1991, her mother killed her father in self-defense. It happened after her father, an [alcoholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism "Alcoholism"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) drunkenly attacked her mother and fired a gun at Charlize and her mother.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-oxygen-14) Theron's mother retrieved her own handgun, shot back and killed him.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-oxygen-14) The shooting was legally adjudged to have been self-defense, and her mother faced no charges.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-biochannel-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-16)

Growing up, Theron felt she did not fit in at school and was teased by other girls.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-WIRED-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-peoplemag1127-17) She was frequently unwell with [jaundice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaundice "Jaundice") throughout childhood and the [antibiotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotics "Antibiotics") she was administered made her upper [incisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incisor "Incisor") baby teeth rot; they had to be surgically removed. Theron's permanent teeth did not grow until she was roughly ten years old.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-teeth-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-19) She attended Putfontein Primary School (Laerskool Putfontein). At 13, Theron was sent to boarding school and began her studies at the National School of the Arts in Johannesburg.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-teeth-18) About her early life in her home country, Theron has said: "I grew up as an only child in South Africa, and there was turmoil in my family, but the surroundings were so great. I was usually barefoot in the dirt: no [Game Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy"), no computers, and we had sanctions, so there were no concerts. This meant you had to entertain yourself."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)

## Career

### 1991–2002: Early work and breakthrough

Although she saw herself as a dancer,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20) Theron left South Africa at age 16 to begin a modeling career in Europe.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-21) That same year, she won a one-year modelling contract[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) at a local competition in [Salerno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salerno "Salerno"), Italy[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-22) and moved with her mother to [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), Italy.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-usaweekend-24) After Theron spent a year modelling throughout Europe, she and her mother moved to the United States; they resided in New York City and [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-usaweekend-24) In New York, she attended the [Joffrey Ballet School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joffrey_Ballet_School "Joffrey Ballet School"), where she trained as a ballet dancer until a knee injury closed this career path.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-indielondon-25) As Theron recalled in 2008:

> I went to New York for three days to model, and then I spent a winter in New York in a friend's windowless basement apartment. I was broke, I was taking class at the Joffrey Ballet, and my knees gave out. I realized I couldn't dance anymore, and I went into a [major depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder "Major depressive disorder"). My mom came over from South Africa and said, "Either you figure out what to do next or you come home, because you can sulk in South Africa".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)

In 1994,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-26) Theron flew to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") on a one-way ticket her mother bought for her; she intended to work in the film industry.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20) During her initial months there, she lived in a motel with the $300 budget that her mother had given her;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) she continued receiving checks from New York and lived "from paycheck to paycheck".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Fast-27) Theron stole bread from a basket in a restaurant to survive.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Fast-27)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) One day, she went to a [Hollywood Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard") bank to cash a few checks, including one her mother had sent to help with the rent;[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-indielondon-25)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) however; the check from her mother was rejected because it was out-of-state and she was not an American citizen.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) Theron argued and pleaded with the [bank teller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_teller "Bank teller") until [talent agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agent "Talent agent") John Crosby,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-indielondon-25) who was the next customer behind her, cashed it for her and gave her his business card.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6)

Crosby introduced Theron to an acting school.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-28) In 1995, she played her first non-speaking film role in the [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_the\_Corn\_III:\_Urban\_Harvest "Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) In Theron's first speaking role, she portrayed [hitwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitwoman "Hitwoman") Helga Svelgen in _[2 Days in the Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2\_Days\_in\_the\_Valley "2 Days in the Valley")_ (1996). Despite the film's mixed reviews, Theron drew attention due to her beauty and to a scene in which she fought [Teri Hatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teri_Hatcher "Teri Hatcher")'s character.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-firing-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-30) Theron feared being [typecast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typecast "Typecast") as characters similar to Helga and recalled being asked to repeat her performance in the film during auditions:[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) "A lot of people were saying, 'You should just hit while the iron's hot' [...] But playing the same part over and over doesn't leave you with any longevity. And I knew it was going to be harder for me, because of what I look like, to branch out to different kinds of roles".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-firing-29)

When auditioning for _[Showgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showgirls "Showgirls")_, Theron was introduced to talent agent J. J. Harris by co-casting director Johanna Ray. She recalled being surprised at how much faith Harris had in her potential. Theron has referred to Harris as her mentor. Harris found scripts and films for Theron in a variety of genres and encouraged her to become a producer. She served as Theron's agent for over 15 years.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23)

Theron's career expanded by the end of the 1990s. In the horror drama _[The Devil's Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Advocate\_(1997\_film) "The Devil's Advocate (1997 film)")_ (1997), which is credited as her break-out film,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-31) Theron starred alongside [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves") and [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino") as the haunted wife of an unusually successful lawyer. She subsequently starred in the adventure film _[Mighty Joe Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mighty\_Joe\_Young\_(1998\_film) "Mighty Joe Young (1998 film)")_ (1998) as the friend and protector of a giant mountain gorilla, and in the drama _[The Cider House Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cider\_House\_Rules "The Cider House Rules")_ (1999), as a woman who seeks an abortion in World War II-era [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) While _Mighty Joe Young_ flopped at the box office,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-32)_The Devil's Advocate_ and _The Cider House Rules_ were commercially successful.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-34) She appeared on the cover of the January 1999 issue of _[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity\_Fair\_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")_ as the "White Hot Venus".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-35) The May 1999 issue of _[Playboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playboy\_(magazine) "Playboy (magazine)")_ magazine also featured Theron on its cover; the photos of Theron used by _Playboy_ had been taken several years earlier when she was an unknown model, and Theron unsuccessfully sued the magazine for publishing them without her consent.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-37)

By the early 2000s, Theron continued to steadily take on roles in films such as _[Reindeer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reindeer\_Games "Reindeer Games")_ (2000), _[The Yards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Yards "The Yards")_ (2000), _[The Legend of Bagger Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Bagger\_Vance "The Legend of Bagger Vance")_ (2000), _[Men of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men\_of\_Honor "Men of Honor")_ (2000), _[Sweet November](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_November\_(2001\_film) "Sweet November (2001 film)")_ (2001), _[The Curse of the Jade Scorpion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Curse\_of\_the\_Jade\_Scorpion "The Curse of the Jade Scorpion")_ (2001), and _[Trapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapped\_(2002\_film) "Trapped (2002 film)")_ (2002), all of which, despite achieving only limited commercial success, helped to establish her as an actress. On this period in her career, Theron remarked: "I kept finding myself in a place where directors would back me but studios didn't. [I began] a love affair with directors, the ones I really, truly admired. I found myself making really bad movies, too. _Reindeer Games_ was not a good movie, but I did it because I loved [director] [John Frankenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Frankenheimer "John Frankenheimer")".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-38)

### 2011–2019: Established actress

Following a two-year hiatus from films, Theron returned to the spotlight in 2011 with the black comedy _[Young Adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Adult\_(film) "Young Adult (film)")_. Directed by Jason Reitman, the film earned critical acclaim, particularly for her performance as a depressed, divorced, alcoholic 37-year-old [ghostwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter"). [Richard Roeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Roeper "Richard Roeper") awarded the film an A grade, stating "Charlize Theron delivers one of the most impressive performances of the year".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-62) She was nominated for a Golden Globe Award and several other awards. Roger Ebert called her one of the best actors working today.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-63)

### 2020–present: Continued success

In 2020, she produced and starred opposite [KiKi Layne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KiKi_Layne "KiKi Layne") in the superhero film _[The Old Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Old\_Guard\_(2020\_film) "The Old Guard (2020 film)")_, directed by [Gina Prince-Bythewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gina_Prince-Bythewood "Gina Prince-Bythewood").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-97) The following year, she reprised her role as Cipher in _[F9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F9\_(film) "F9 (film)")_, originally set for release on 22 May 2020,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-98) before its delay to June 2021 due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-99)

In 2022, Theron appeared in several projects. Upon the film's release in May, it was revealed that Theron would portray the character [Clea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clea_Strange "Clea Strange") in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") (MCU), beginning with her debut in the [mid-credits scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-credits_scene "Mid-credits scene") of the superhero film _[Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor\_Strange\_in\_the\_Multiverse\_of\_Madness "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness")_.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-100) She played Lady Lesso in the fantasy [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") film _[The School for Good and Evil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_School\_for\_Good\_and\_Evil\_(film) "The School for Good and Evil (film)")_[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-101) and filmed a [cameo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance") in the third season opener of _[The Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boys\_(TV\_series) "The Boys (TV series)")_ as an actress playing Stormfront.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-102)

In 2023, Theron reprised her role as Cipher in _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_X "Fast X")_ and executive produced the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") documentary series _[Last Call: When a Serial Killer Stalked Queer New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last\_Call:\_When\_a\_Serial\_Killer\_Stalked\_Queer\_New\_York "Last Call: When a Serial Killer Stalked Queer New York")_ about a serial killer preying on gay men.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-103) In 2024, she was cast in [Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan "Christopher Nolan")'s _[The Odyssey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Odyssey\_(2026\_film) "The Odyssey (2026 film)")_ (2026) as the goddess [Calypso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calypso_(mythology) "Calypso (mythology)").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-104)

## Influences and process

Theron is inspired by actresses [Susan Sarandon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Sarandon "Susan Sarandon") and [Sigourney Weaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigourney_Weaver "Sigourney Weaver").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) She has described her admiration for [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks") as a "love affair" and watched many of his films throughout her youth.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-105)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) Hollywood actors were not featured in magazines in South Africa so she did not know how famous he was until she moved to the United States,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) which has been inferred as a factor of her "down-to-earth" attitude to fame.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-106) After filming for _[That Thing You Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That\_Thing\_You\_Do! "That Thing You Do!")_ finished, Theron got Hanks' [autograph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autograph "Autograph") on her script.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-107) She later presented him his [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Cecil B. DeMille Award") in 2020, in which Hanks revealed that he had a mutual admiration for Theron's career since the day he met her.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-108)

In 2019, Theron spoke about her method of working on roles. Creating a physical identity together with the emotional part of the character, she said, is "a great tool set that adds on to everything else you were already doing as an actor. It's a case-by-case thing, but there is, to me, this beautiful thing that happens when you can get both sides: the exterior and interior. It's a really powerful dynamic". When preparing for a role, "I almost treat it like studying. I will find space where I am alone, where I can be focused, where there's nobody in my house, and I can really just sit down and study and play and look at my face and hear my voice and walk around and be a fucking idiot and my dogs are the only ones who are seeing that".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-109)

## Other ventures

### Activism

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Crystal_Award_Ceremony_-_Exploring_Arts_in_Society_Charlize_Theron.jpg/250px-Crystal_Award_Ceremony_-_Exploring_Arts_in_Society_Charlize_Theron.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Crystal_Award_Ceremony_-_Exploring_Arts_in_Society_Charlize_Theron.jpg)

Theron speaking at a meeting of the [World Economic Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Economic_Forum "World Economic Forum") in 2013

The Charlize Theron Africa Outreach Project (CTAOP) was created in 2007 by Theron, in an effort to support African youth in the fight against [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS"). By November 2017, CTAOP had raised more than $6.3 million to support African organizations working on the ground.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-110)

In 2008, Theron was named a [United Nations Messenger of Peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Messenger_of_Peace "United Nations Messenger of Peace").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-112) In his citation, [Ban Ki-moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Ki-moon "Ban Ki-moon") said of Theron: "You have consistently dedicated yourself to improving the lives of women and children in South Africa, and to preventing and stopping violence against women and girls."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-113) She recorded a public service announcement in 2014 as part of the UN's "Stop Rape Now" program.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-114)

In December 2009, CTAOP and [Toms Shoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toms_Shoes "Toms Shoes") partnered to create a limited edition unisex shoe. The shoe was made from vegan materials and inspired by the African [baobab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adansonia_digitata "Adansonia digitata") tree, the silhouette of which was embroidered on blue and orange canvas. Ten thousand pairs were given to destitute children, and a portion of the proceeds went to CTAOP.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-115)

In 2020, CTAOP partnered with [Parfums Christian Dior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parfums_Christian_Dior "Parfums Christian Dior") to create Dior Stands With Women, an initiative that includes [Cara Delevingne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cara_Delevingne "Cara Delevingne"), [Yalitza Aparicio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalitza_Aparicio "Yalitza Aparicio"), [Paloma Elsesser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paloma_Elsesser "Paloma Elsesser"), and others, to encourage women to be assertive by documenting their journey, challenges and accomplishments.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-116)

Theron is involved in [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights") organizations and has marched in [pro-choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-choice "Pro-choice") rallies.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-117)

Theron is a supporter of [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage") and attended a march and rally to support that in [Fresno, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno,_California "Fresno, California"), on 30 May 2009.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-118) She publicly stated that she refused to get married until same-sex marriage became legal in the United States, saying:

> I don't want to get married because right now the institution of marriage feels very one-sided, and I want to live in a country where we all have equal rights. I think it would be exactly the same if we were married, but for me to go through that kind of ceremony, because I have so many friends who are gays and lesbians who would so badly want to get married, that I wouldn't be able to sleep with myself....[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-119)

Theron further elaborated on her stance in a June 2011 interview on _[Piers Morgan Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piers\_Morgan\_Tonight "Piers Morgan Tonight")_. She stated: "I do have a problem with the fact that our government hasn't stepped up enough to make this federal, to make [gay marriage] legal. I think everybody has that right".[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-120)

In March 2014, CTAOP was among the charities that benefited from the annual [Fame and Philanthropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fame_and_Philanthropy "Fame and Philanthropy") fundraising event on the night of the [86th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/86th_Academy_Awards "86th Academy Awards"). Theron was an honoured guest along with Halle Berry and keynote speaker [James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-121)

In 2015, Theron signed an open letter which [One Campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Campaign "One Campaign") had been collecting signatures for; the letter was addressed to [Angela Merkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Merkel "Angela Merkel") and [Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nkosazana_Dlamini-Zuma "Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma"), urging them to focus on women as they serve as the head of the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G7 "G7") in Germany and the [AU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") in South Africa respectively, which will start to set the priorities in development funding before a main UN summit in September 2015 that will establish new development goals for the generation.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-122) In August 2017, she visited South Africa with [Trevor Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Noah "Trevor Noah") and made a donation to the South African charity Life Choices.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-123) In 2018, she gave a speech about AIDS prevention at the 22nd International AIDS Conference in Amsterdam, organized by the [International AIDS Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_AIDS_Society "International AIDS Society").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-panther-124) In June 2019, Theron participated in the [LA Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Pride "Los Angeles Pride") in [West Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Hollywood "West Hollywood"), California, marching in support of [LGBTQ+ rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ+_rights "LGBTQ+ rights") during [Pride Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Month "Pride Month").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-125)

On 22 June 2022, it was announced that Theron and [Sheryl Lee Ralph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheryl_Lee_Ralph "Sheryl Lee Ralph") would receive the Elizabeth Taylor Commitment to End AIDS Award for their commitment to raising awareness of HIV at the Elizabeth Taylor Ball to End AIDS fundraising gala.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-126) She participated in the [2026 Winter Olympics opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2026 Winter Olympics opening ceremony"), held at [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro") stadium in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), where she delivered a message of peace and unity, speaking against war and emphasizing harmony and global solidarity.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-127)

### Endorsements

Having signed a deal with [John Galliano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Galliano "John Galliano") in 2004, Theron replaced Estonian model [Tiiu Kuik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiiu_Kuik "Tiiu Kuik") as the spokeswoman in the [J'Adore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J'Adore_(fragrance) "J'Adore (fragrance)") advertisements by [Christian Dior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dior "Dior").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-128) In June 2024, Dior announced Theron would no longer be the face of J'Adore and would be replaced by [Barbadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados "Barbados") singer and businesswoman [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-129) From October 2005 to December 2006, Theron earned US$3 million for the use of her image in a worldwide print media advertising campaign for Raymond Weil watches.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-smoke-130) In February 2006, she and her production company were sued by Weil for breach of contract.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-smoke-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-131) The lawsuit was settled on 4 November 2008.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-132) In 2018, Theron joined [Brad Pitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt"), [Daniel Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Wu "Daniel Wu") and [Adam Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Driver "Adam Driver") as brand ambassadors for [Breitling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breitling_SA "Breitling SA"), dubbed the Breitling Cinema Squad.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-134)

## Personal life

In 2007, Theron became a naturalised [citizen of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship_of_the_United_States "Citizenship of the United States"),[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-cbs-135) while retaining her [South African citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_nationality_law "South African nationality law").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-136)

Theron adopted two young daughters.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-138) She has been interested in adoption since childhood, when she became aware of orphanages and the overflowing numbers of children in them.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23) In April 2019, Theron revealed that one of her daughters, then seven years old, is a [transgender girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans_woman "Trans woman"). She said of her daughters, "They were born who they are and exactly where in the world both of them get to find themselves as they grow up, and who they want to be, is not for me to decide".[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-139)

Theron said in 2018 that she went to therapy in her thirties because of anger, discovering that it was due to her frustration growing up during [South Africa's apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid_in_South_Africa "Apartheid in South Africa"),[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-panther-124)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23) which ended when she was 15.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23)

Theron is a longtime fan of the English band [Depeche Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depeche_Mode "Depeche Mode") and was the presenter for their [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") induction in 2020.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-140)

### Relationships

Theron's first public relationship was with actor [Craig Bierko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Bierko "Craig Bierko"), whom she dated from 1995 to 1997.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-142)

Theron was in a three-year relationship with singer [Stephan Jenkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephan_Jenkins "Stephan Jenkins") until October 2001. Some of [Third Eye Blind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Eye_Blind "Third Eye Blind")'s third album, _[Out of the Vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out\_of\_the\_Vein "Out of the Vein")_, explores the emotions Jenkins experienced as a result of their breakup.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Guthrie-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-144)

Theron was in a relationship with Irish actor [Stuart Townsend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Townsend "Stuart Townsend") from 2001 to 2009 after meeting him on the set of _[Trapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapped\_(2002\_film) "Trapped (2002 film)")_. The couple lived together in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") and Ireland.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-146)

In December 2013, Theron began dating American actor [Sean Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Penn "Sean Penn").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-147) The relationship ended in June 2015.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-148) There were reports they were engaged, which Theron strongly denied, adding that the relationship had ended before it ever became serious.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-149) Theron starred in Penn's film _The Last Face_ (2016), which they filmed while still a couple.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-:0-150)

In July 2017, Theron revealed that she had had [same-sex experiences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_practices_between_women "Sexual practices between women") when she was younger, describing them as part of exploring her sexuality during her youth, but added that she was ultimately attracted primarily to men.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-151) In July 2025, she disclosed that she had recently had a one-night stand with a 26-year-old man, saying that the experience had given her a greater sense of freedom in her forties and reaffirming her preference for remaining single while dating casually.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-152) In April 2026, Theron said that she did not think she would ever want to live with a romantic partner again, explaining that she had grown accustomed to her independence as a single mother and was focused on her family.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-153)

### Health concerns

During her first modeling job in [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco") at age 16, Theron recalled being thrown from a camel during a photo shoot after the animal became unruly, striking her in the face and dislocating her jaw.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-154)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-155) Theron often quips that she has more injuries on sets that are not action films;[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tullyGMA-156) however, while filming _[Æon Flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%86on\_Flux\_(film) "Æon Flux (film)")_ in Berlin, Theron suffered a [herniated disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_disc_herniation "Spinal disc herniation") in her neck, caused by a fall while filming a series of back [handsprings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handspring_(gymnastics) "Handspring (gymnastics)"). It required her to wear a [neck brace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_collar "Cervical collar") for a month.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-157) Her thumb [ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligament "Ligament") tore during filming of _The Old Guard_ when her thumb caught in another actor's jacket during a fight scene, which required three operations and six months in a thumb brace.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-158)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-injuries-159) During the filming of _[Atomic Blonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic\_Blonde "Atomic Blonde")_ she broke teeth from clenching her jaw,[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-160) and had dental surgery to remove them: "I had the removal and I had to put a donor bone in there to heal until I came back, and then I had another surgery to put a metal screw in there."[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-injuries-159)

Outside of action films, she had a herniated disk in her lower back as she filmed _[Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tully\_(2018\_film) "Tully (2018 film)")_ and suffered from a depression-like state, which she theorized was the result of the [processed food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processed_food "Processed food") she had to eat for her character's [post-natal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-natal "Post-natal") body.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-161) In July 2009, she was diagnosed with a serious [stomach virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastroenteritis "Gastroenteritis"), thought to be contracted while overseas.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-162)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-163) While filming _[The Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Road\_(2009\_film) "The Road (2009 film)")_, Theron injured her [vocal cords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_cords "Vocal cords") while screaming during the [labour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childbirth "Childbirth") scenes.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-164) When promoting _[Long Shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Shot\_(2019\_film) "Long Shot (2019 film)")_, she revealed that she laughed so hard at _[Borat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borat "Borat")_ that her neck locked for five days.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-metro-165) She added that on the set of _Long Shot_ she "ended up in the [ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_room "Emergency room")" after knocking her head against a bench behind her when she was putting on [knee pads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee_pad "Knee pad").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-metro-165)

**Charlize Theron** ([/ʃ ɑːr ˈ l iː z ˈ θ ɛr ə n/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_shar-LEEZ THERR-ən_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-pron2-1)Afrikaans:[[ʃarˈlis ˈtrɔn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Afrikaans "Help:IPA/Afrikaans");[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-pron1-2) born 7 August 1975) is a South African[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Nationality-3) and American actress and producer. One of the world's highest-paid actresses,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-forbes19-4)[her accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_Charlize_Theron "List of accolades received by Charlize Theron") include an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") and a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award"), in addition to nominations for three [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs") and two [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Awards "Emmy Awards").

Theron came to international prominence in the 1990s by playing the leading lady in the [Hollywood films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States")_[The Devil's Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Advocate\_(1997\_film) "The Devil's Advocate (1997 film)")_ (1997), _[Mighty Joe Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mighty\_Joe\_Young\_(1998\_film) "Mighty Joe Young (1998 film)")_ (1998), and _[The Cider House Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cider\_House\_Rules "The Cider House Rules")_ (1999). She received critical acclaim for her portrayal of serial killer [Aileen Wuornos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aileen_Wuornos "Aileen Wuornos") in _[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_(2003\_film) "Monster (2003 film)")_ (2003), for which she won the [Silver Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Bear_for_Best_Actress "Silver Bear for Best Actress") and [Academy Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress"), becoming [the first South African to win an acting Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_African_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Best_Actress "List of African Academy Award winners and nominees"). She was nominated twice more for the Oscar for portraying a sexually abused woman seeking justice in the drama _[North Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_Country\_(film) "North Country (film)")_ (2005) and [Megyn Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megyn_Kelly "Megyn Kelly") in the biographical drama _[Bombshell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombshell\_(2019\_film) "Bombshell (2019 film)")_ (2019). She received praise for playing troubled women in [Jason Reitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Reitman "Jason Reitman")'s comedy-dramas _[Young Adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Adult\_(film) "Young Adult (film)")_ (2011) and _[Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tully\_(2018\_film) "Tully (2018 film)")_ (2018).

Theron has starred in several commercially successful action films, including _[The Italian Job](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Italian\_Job\_(2003\_film) "The Italian Job (2003 film)")_ (2003), _[Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock\_(film) "Hancock (film)")_ (2008), _[Prometheus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prometheus\_(2012\_film) "Prometheus (2012 film)")_ (2012), _[Mad Max: Fury Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Max:\_Fury\_Road "Mad Max: Fury Road")_ (2015), _[Atomic Blonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic\_Blonde "Atomic Blonde")_ (2017), and _[The Old Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Old\_Guard\_(2020\_film) "The Old Guard (2020 film)")_ (2020), as well as several _[Fast & Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_&\_Furious "Fast & Furious")_ installments: _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ (2017), _[F9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F9\_(film) "F9 (film)")_ (2021), and _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_X "Fast X")_ (2023). On television, she earned a nomination for the [Primetime Emmy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Supporting_Actress_in_a_Limited_or_Anthology_Series_or_Movie "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie") for her portrayal of [Britt Ekland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britt_Ekland "Britt Ekland") in the biographical film _[The Life and Death of Peter Sellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Life\_and\_Death\_of\_Peter\_Sellers "The Life and Death of Peter Sellers")_ (2004).

Since the early 2000s, Theron has ventured into film production with her company [Denver and Delilah Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_and_Delilah_Productions "Denver and Delilah Productions"). She has produced numerous films, many in which she had a starring role, including _[The Burning Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Burning\_Plain "The Burning Plain")_ (2008), _[Dark Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark\_Places\_(2015\_film) "Dark Places (2015 film)")_ (2015), and _[Long Shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Shot\_(2019\_film) "Long Shot (2019 film)")_ (2019). Theron became an American citizen in 2007, while retaining her South African citizenship. In 2016, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ named her one of the [100 most influential people in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100").

## Early life

Charlize Theron was born in South Africa, in [Benoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng "Benoni, Gauteng") in [Transvaal Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transvaal_Province "Transvaal Province") ([Gauteng Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng_Province "Gauteng Province") since 1994).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-5) She is the only child of [road builders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_construction "Road construction")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) Gerda ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9e "Née") Maritz)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):16-18 and Charles Theron.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):16-18, 34 Her great-granduncle was [Second Boer War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Boer_War "Second Boer War") military leader [Daniel Theron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Theron "Daniel Theron").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):14 She is from an [Afrikaner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaner "Afrikaner") family, and her ancestry includes Dutch as well as French and German. Her French forebears were early [Huguenots in South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huguenots_in_South_Africa "Huguenots in South Africa").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-bookrefp18-7):14 Although Theron is fluent in English, her [first language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_language "First language") is [Afrikaans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaans "Afrikaans").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-9) She grew up on her parents' farm in Benoni, near [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-WIRED-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-13)

When Theron was 15, on 21 June 1991, her mother killed her father in self-defense. It happened after her father, an [alcoholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism "Alcoholism"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) drunkenly attacked her mother and fired a gun at Charlize and her mother.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-oxygen-14) Theron's mother retrieved her own handgun, shot back and killed him.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-oxygen-14) The shooting was legally adjudged to have been self-defense, and her mother faced no charges.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-biochannel-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-16)

Growing up, Theron felt she did not fit in at school and was teased by other girls.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-WIRED-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-peoplemag1127-17) She was frequently unwell with [jaundice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaundice "Jaundice") throughout childhood and the [antibiotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotics "Antibiotics") she was administered made her upper [incisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incisor "Incisor") baby teeth rot; they had to be surgically removed. Theron's permanent teeth did not grow until she was roughly ten years old.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-teeth-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-19) She attended Putfontein Primary School (Laerskool Putfontein). At 13, Theron was sent to boarding school and began her studies at the National School of the Arts in Johannesburg.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-teeth-18) About her early life in her home country, Theron has said: "I grew up as an only child in South Africa, and there was turmoil in my family, but the surroundings were so great. I was usually barefoot in the dirt: no [Game Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy "Game Boy"), no computers, and we had sanctions, so there were no concerts. This meant you had to entertain yourself."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)

## Career

### 1991–2002: Early work and breakthrough

Although she saw herself as a dancer,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20) Theron left South Africa at age 16 to begin a modeling career in Europe.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-21) That same year, she won a one-year modelling contract[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) at a local competition in [Salerno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salerno "Salerno"), Italy[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-22) and moved with her mother to [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), Italy.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-usaweekend-24) After Theron spent a year modelling throughout Europe, she and her mother moved to the United States; they resided in New York City and [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-usaweekend-24) In New York, she attended the [Joffrey Ballet School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joffrey_Ballet_School "Joffrey Ballet School"), where she trained as a ballet dancer until a knee injury closed this career path.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-indielondon-25) As Theron recalled in 2008:

> I went to New York for three days to model, and then I spent a winter in New York in a friend's windowless basement apartment. I was broke, I was taking class at the Joffrey Ballet, and my knees gave out. I realized I couldn't dance anymore, and I went into a [major depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder "Major depressive disorder"). My mom came over from South Africa and said, "Either you figure out what to do next or you come home, because you can sulk in South Africa".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20)

In 1994,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-26) Theron flew to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") on a one-way ticket her mother bought for her; she intended to work in the film industry.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-CharAngel-20) During her initial months there, she lived in a motel with the $300 budget that her mother had given her;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) she continued receiving checks from New York and lived "from paycheck to paycheck".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Fast-27) Theron stole bread from a basket in a restaurant to survive.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Fast-27)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) One day, she went to a [Hollywood Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard") bank to cash a few checks, including one her mother had sent to help with the rent;[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-indielondon-25)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) however; the check from her mother was rejected because it was out-of-state and she was not an American citizen.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) Theron argued and pleaded with the [bank teller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_teller "Bank teller") until [talent agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agent "Talent agent") John Crosby,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-indielondon-25) who was the next customer behind her, cashed it for her and gave her his business card.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6)

Crosby introduced Theron to an acting school.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-28) In 1995, she played her first non-speaking film role in the [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_the\_Corn\_III:\_Urban\_Harvest "Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) In Theron's first speaking role, she portrayed [hitwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitwoman "Hitwoman") Helga Svelgen in _[2 Days in the Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2\_Days\_in\_the\_Valley "2 Days in the Valley")_ (1996). Despite the film's mixed reviews, Theron drew attention due to her beauty and to a scene in which she fought [Teri Hatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teri_Hatcher "Teri Hatcher")'s character.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-firing-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-30) Theron feared being [typecast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typecast "Typecast") as characters similar to Helga and recalled being asked to repeat her performance in the film during auditions:[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) "A lot of people were saying, 'You should just hit while the iron's hot' [...] But playing the same part over and over doesn't leave you with any longevity. And I knew it was going to be harder for me, because of what I look like, to branch out to different kinds of roles".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-firing-29)

When auditioning for _[Showgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showgirls "Showgirls")_, Theron was introduced to talent agent J. J. Harris by co-casting director Johanna Ray. She recalled being surprised at how much faith Harris had in her potential. Theron has referred to Harris as her mentor. Harris found scripts and films for Theron in a variety of genres and encouraged her to become a producer. She served as Theron's agent for over 15 years.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23)

Theron's career expanded by the end of the 1990s. In the horror drama _[The Devil's Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Advocate\_(1997\_film) "The Devil's Advocate (1997 film)")_ (1997), which is credited as her break-out film,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-31) Theron starred alongside [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves") and [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino") as the haunted wife of an unusually successful lawyer. She subsequently starred in the adventure film _[Mighty Joe Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mighty\_Joe\_Young\_(1998\_film) "Mighty Joe Young (1998 film)")_ (1998) as the friend and protector of a giant mountain gorilla, and in the drama _[The Cider House Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cider\_House\_Rules "The Cider House Rules")_ (1999), as a woman who seeks an abortion in World War II-era [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tca-10) While _Mighty Joe Young_ flopped at the box office,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-32)_The Devil's Advocate_ and _The Cider House Rules_ were commercially successful.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-34) She appeared on the cover of the January 1999 issue of _[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity\_Fair\_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")_ as the "White Hot Venus".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-35) The May 1999 issue of _[Playboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playboy\_(magazine) "Playboy (magazine)")_ magazine also featured Theron on its cover; the photos of Theron used by _Playboy_ had been taken several years earlier when she was an unknown model, and Theron unsuccessfully sued the magazine for publishing them without her consent.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-37)

By the early 2000s, Theron continued to steadily take on roles in films such as _[Reindeer Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reindeer\_Games "Reindeer Games")_ (2000), _[The Yards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Yards "The Yards")_ (2000), _[The Legend of Bagger Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Legend\_of\_Bagger\_Vance "The Legend of Bagger Vance")_ (2000), _[Men of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men\_of\_Honor "Men of Honor")_ (2000), _[Sweet November](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_November\_(2001\_film) "Sweet November (2001 film)")_ (2001), _[The Curse of the Jade Scorpion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Curse\_of\_the\_Jade\_Scorpion "The Curse of the Jade Scorpion")_ (2001), and _[Trapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapped\_(2002\_film) "Trapped (2002 film)")_ (2002), all of which, despite achieving only limited commercial success, helped to establish her as an actress. On this period in her career, Theron remarked: "I kept finding myself in a place where directors would back me but studios didn't. [I began] a love affair with directors, the ones I really, truly admired. I found myself making really bad movies, too. _Reindeer Games_ was not a good movie, but I did it because I loved [director] [John Frankenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Frankenheimer "John Frankenheimer")".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-38)

### 2011–2019: Established actress

Following a two-year hiatus from films, Theron returned to the spotlight in 2011 with the black comedy _[Young Adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Adult\_(film) "Young Adult (film)")_. Directed by Jason Reitman, the film earned critical acclaim, particularly for her performance as a depressed, divorced, alcoholic 37-year-old [ghostwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter"). [Richard Roeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Roeper "Richard Roeper") awarded the film an A grade, stating "Charlize Theron delivers one of the most impressive performances of the year".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-62) She was nominated for a Golden Globe Award and several other awards. Roger Ebert called her one of the best actors working today.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-63)

## Influences and process

Theron is inspired by actresses [Susan Sarandon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Sarandon "Susan Sarandon") and [Sigourney Weaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigourney_Weaver "Sigourney Weaver").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) She has described her admiration for [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks") as a "love affair" and watched many of his films throughout her youth.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-105)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) Hollywood actors were not featured in magazines in South Africa so she did not know how famous he was until she moved to the United States,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-SAGinterview-6) which has been inferred as a factor of her "down-to-earth" attitude to fame.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-106) After filming for _[That Thing You Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That\_Thing\_You\_Do! "That Thing You Do!")_ finished, Theron got Hanks' [autograph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autograph "Autograph") on her script.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-107) She later presented him his [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Cecil B. DeMille Award") in 2020, in which Hanks revealed that he had a mutual admiration for Theron's career since the day he met her.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-108)

In 2019, Theron spoke about her method of working on roles. Creating a physical identity together with the emotional part of the character, she said, is "a great tool set that adds on to everything else you were already doing as an actor. It's a case-by-case thing, but there is, to me, this beautiful thing that happens when you can get both sides: the exterior and interior. It's a really powerful dynamic". When preparing for a role, "I almost treat it like studying. I will find space where I am alone, where I can be focused, where there's nobody in my house, and I can really just sit down and study and play and look at my face and hear my voice and walk around and be a fucking idiot and my dogs are the only ones who are seeing that".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-109)
