The Charlize Theron Africa Outreach Project (CTAOP) was created in 2007 by Theron, in an effort to support African youth in the fight against [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS"). By November 2017, CTAOP had raised more than $6.3 million to support African organizations working on the ground.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-110)

In 2008, Theron was named a [United Nations Messenger of Peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Messenger_of_Peace "United Nations Messenger of Peace").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-112) In his citation, [Ban Ki-moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ban_Ki-moon "Ban Ki-moon") said of Theron: "You have consistently dedicated yourself to improving the lives of women and children in South Africa, and to preventing and stopping violence against women and girls."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-113) She recorded a public service announcement in 2014 as part of the UN's "Stop Rape Now" program.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-114)

In December 2009, CTAOP and [Toms Shoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toms_Shoes "Toms Shoes") partnered to create a limited edition unisex shoe. The shoe was made from vegan materials and inspired by the African [baobab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adansonia_digitata "Adansonia digitata") tree, the silhouette of which was embroidered on blue and orange canvas. Ten thousand pairs were given to destitute children, and a portion of the proceeds went to CTAOP.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-115)

In 2020, CTAOP partnered with [Parfums Christian Dior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parfums_Christian_Dior "Parfums Christian Dior") to create Dior Stands With Women, an initiative that includes [Cara Delevingne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cara_Delevingne "Cara Delevingne"), [Yalitza Aparicio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalitza_Aparicio "Yalitza Aparicio"), [Paloma Elsesser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paloma_Elsesser "Paloma Elsesser"), and others, to encourage women to be assertive by documenting their journey, challenges and accomplishments.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-116)

Theron is involved in [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights") organizations and has marched in [pro-choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-choice "Pro-choice") rallies.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-117)

Theron is a supporter of [same-sex marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage "Same-sex marriage") and attended a march and rally to support that in [Fresno, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno,_California "Fresno, California"), on 30 May 2009.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-118) She publicly stated that she refused to get married until same-sex marriage became legal in the United States, saying:

> I don't want to get married because right now the institution of marriage feels very one-sided, and I want to live in a country where we all have equal rights. I think it would be exactly the same if we were married, but for me to go through that kind of ceremony, because I have so many friends who are gays and lesbians who would so badly want to get married, that I wouldn't be able to sleep with myself....[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-119)

Theron further elaborated on her stance in a June 2011 interview on _[Piers Morgan Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piers\_Morgan\_Tonight "Piers Morgan Tonight")_. She stated: "I do have a problem with the fact that our government hasn't stepped up enough to make this federal, to make [gay marriage] legal. I think everybody has that right".[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-120)

In March 2014, CTAOP was among the charities that benefited from the annual [Fame and Philanthropy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fame_and_Philanthropy "Fame and Philanthropy") fundraising event on the night of the [86th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/86th_Academy_Awards "86th Academy Awards"). Theron was an honoured guest along with Halle Berry and keynote speaker [James Cameron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cameron "James Cameron").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-121)

In 2015, Theron signed an open letter which [One Campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Campaign "One Campaign") had been collecting signatures for; the letter was addressed to [Angela Merkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Merkel "Angela Merkel") and [Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nkosazana_Dlamini-Zuma "Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma"), urging them to focus on women as they serve as the head of the [G7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G7 "G7") in Germany and the [AU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Union "African Union") in South Africa respectively, which will start to set the priorities in development funding before a main UN summit in September 2015 that will establish new development goals for the generation.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-122) In August 2017, she visited South Africa with [Trevor Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Noah "Trevor Noah") and made a donation to the South African charity Life Choices.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-123) In 2018, she gave a speech about AIDS prevention at the 22nd International AIDS Conference in Amsterdam, organized by the [International AIDS Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_AIDS_Society "International AIDS Society").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-panther-124) In June 2019, Theron participated in the [LA Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Pride "Los Angeles Pride") in [West Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Hollywood "West Hollywood"), California, marching in support of [LGBTQ+ rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ+_rights "LGBTQ+ rights") during [Pride Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Month "Pride Month").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-125)

On 22 June 2022, it was announced that Theron and [Sheryl Lee Ralph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheryl_Lee_Ralph "Sheryl Lee Ralph") would receive the Elizabeth Taylor Commitment to End AIDS Award for their commitment to raising awareness of HIV at the Elizabeth Taylor Ball to End AIDS fundraising gala.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-126) She participated in the [2026 Winter Olympics opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2026 Winter Olympics opening ceremony"), held at [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro") stadium in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), where she delivered a message of peace and unity, speaking against war and emphasizing harmony and global solidarity.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-127)

### Endorsements

Having signed a deal with [John Galliano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Galliano "John Galliano") in 2004, Theron replaced Estonian model [Tiiu Kuik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiiu_Kuik "Tiiu Kuik") as the spokeswoman in the [J'Adore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J'Adore_(fragrance) "J'Adore (fragrance)") advertisements by [Christian Dior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dior "Dior").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-128) In June 2024, Dior announced Theron would no longer be the face of J'Adore and would be replaced by [Barbadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados "Barbados") singer and businesswoman [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-129) From October 2005 to December 2006, Theron earned US$3 million for the use of her image in a worldwide print media advertising campaign for Raymond Weil watches.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-smoke-130) In February 2006, she and her production company were sued by Weil for breach of contract.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-smoke-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-131) The lawsuit was settled on 4 November 2008.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-132) In 2018, Theron joined [Brad Pitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt"), [Daniel Wu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Wu "Daniel Wu") and [Adam Driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Driver "Adam Driver") as brand ambassadors for [Breitling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breitling_SA "Breitling SA"), dubbed the Breitling Cinema Squad.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-134)

## Personal life

In 2007, Theron became a naturalised [citizen of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship_of_the_United_States "Citizenship of the United States"),[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-cbs-135) while retaining her [South African citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_nationality_law "South African nationality law").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-136)

Theron adopted two young daughters.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-138) She has been interested in adoption since childhood, when she became aware of orphanages and the overflowing numbers of children in them.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23) In April 2019, Theron revealed that one of her daughters, then seven years old, is a [transgender girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans_woman "Trans woman"). She said of her daughters, "They were born who they are and exactly where in the world both of them get to find themselves as they grow up, and who they want to be, is not for me to decide".[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-139)

Theron said in 2018 that she went to therapy in her thirties because of anger, discovering that it was due to her frustration growing up during [South Africa's apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid_in_South_Africa "Apartheid in South Africa"),[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-panther-124)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23) which ended when she was 15.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-FiveThings-23)

Theron is a longtime fan of the English band [Depeche Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depeche_Mode "Depeche Mode") and was the presenter for their [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") induction in 2020.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-140)

### Relationships

Theron's first public relationship was with actor [Craig Bierko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Bierko "Craig Bierko"), whom she dated from 1995 to 1997.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-142)

Theron was in a three-year relationship with singer [Stephan Jenkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephan_Jenkins "Stephan Jenkins") until October 2001. Some of [Third Eye Blind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Eye_Blind "Third Eye Blind")'s third album, _[Out of the Vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out\_of\_the\_Vein "Out of the Vein")_, explores the emotions Jenkins experienced as a result of their breakup.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-Guthrie-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-144)

Theron was in a relationship with Irish actor [Stuart Townsend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Townsend "Stuart Townsend") from 2001 to 2009 after meeting him on the set of _[Trapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapped\_(2002\_film) "Trapped (2002 film)")_. The couple lived together in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") and Ireland.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-146)

In December 2013, Theron began dating American actor [Sean Penn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Penn "Sean Penn").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-147) The relationship ended in June 2015.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-148) There were reports they were engaged, which Theron strongly denied, adding that the relationship had ended before it ever became serious.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-149) Theron starred in Penn's film _The Last Face_ (2016), which they filmed while still a couple.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-:0-150)

In July 2017, Theron revealed that she had had [same-sex experiences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_practices_between_women "Sexual practices between women") when she was younger, describing them as part of exploring her sexuality during her youth, but added that she was ultimately attracted primarily to men.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-151) In July 2025, she disclosed that she had recently had a one-night stand with a 26-year-old man, saying that the experience had given her a greater sense of freedom in her forties and reaffirming her preference for remaining single while dating casually.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-152) In April 2026, Theron said that she did not think she would ever want to live with a romantic partner again, explaining that she had grown accustomed to her independence as a single mother and was focused on her family.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-153)

### Health concerns

During her first modeling job in [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco") at age 16, Theron recalled being thrown from a camel during a photo shoot after the animal became unruly, striking her in the face and dislocating her jaw.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-154)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-155) Theron often quips that she has more injuries on sets that are not action films;[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-tullyGMA-156) however, while filming _[Æon Flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%86on\_Flux\_(film) "Æon Flux (film)")_ in Berlin, Theron suffered a [herniated disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_disc_herniation "Spinal disc herniation") in her neck, caused by a fall while filming a series of back [handsprings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handspring_(gymnastics) "Handspring (gymnastics)"). It required her to wear a [neck brace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_collar "Cervical collar") for a month.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-157) Her thumb [ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligament "Ligament") tore during filming of _The Old Guard_ when her thumb caught in another actor's jacket during a fight scene, which required three operations and six months in a thumb brace.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-158)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-injuries-159) During the filming of _[Atomic Blonde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic\_Blonde "Atomic Blonde")_ she broke teeth from clenching her jaw,[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-160) and had dental surgery to remove them: "I had the removal and I had to put a donor bone in there to heal until I came back, and then I had another surgery to put a metal screw in there."[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-injuries-159)

Outside of action films, she had a herniated disk in her lower back as she filmed _[Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tully\_(2018\_film) "Tully (2018 film)")_ and suffered from a depression-like state, which she theorized was the result of the [processed food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processed_food "Processed food") she had to eat for her character's [post-natal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-natal "Post-natal") body.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-161) In July 2009, she was diagnosed with a serious [stomach virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastroenteritis "Gastroenteritis"), thought to be contracted while overseas.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-162)[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-163) While filming _[The Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Road\_(2009\_film) "The Road (2009 film)")_, Theron injured her [vocal cords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_cords "Vocal cords") while screaming during the [labour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childbirth "Childbirth") scenes.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-164) When promoting _[Long Shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Shot\_(2019\_film) "Long Shot (2019 film)")_, she revealed that she laughed so hard at _[Borat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borat "Borat")_ that her neck locked for five days.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-metro-165) She added that on the set of _Long Shot_ she "ended up in the [ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_room "Emergency room")" after knocking her head against a bench behind her when she was putting on [knee pads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee_pad "Knee pad").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron#cite_note-metro-165)

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_Gauteng#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

Charlize Theron is a South African and American actress and producer who made her film debut in an uncredited role as a follower of a cult in the 1995 horror film _[Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_the\_Corn\_III:\_Urban\_Harvest "Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-EW-2) Theron followed this with appearances as a hitman's girlfriend in _[2 Days in the Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2\_Days\_in\_the\_Valley "2 Days in the Valley")_,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-3) a waitress in the romantic comedy _[Trial and Error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial\_and\_Error\_(1997\_film) "Trial and Error (1997 film)")_ (1997),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-trial-4) and a woman plagued with demonic visions in the mystery thriller _[The Devil's Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Advocate\_(1997\_film) "The Devil's Advocate (1997 film)")_ (1997) with [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves") and [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-5) She appeared in the science fiction thriller _[The Astronaut's Wife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Astronaut's\_Wife "The Astronaut's Wife")_ with [Johnny Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp"), and [Lasse Hallström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasse_Hallstr%C3%B6m "Lasse Hallström")'s _[The Cider House Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cider\_House\_Rules "The Cider House Rules")_ (both in 1999). For her portrayal of serial killer [Aileen Wuornos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aileen_Wuornos "Aileen Wuornos") in the crime drama _[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_(2003\_film) "Monster (2003 film)")_ (2003), Theron received the [Academy Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-6) the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture– Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-7) and the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Female_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-8) The following year, she played Swedish entertainer [Britt Ekland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britt_Ekland "Britt Ekland") in the biographical film _[The Life and Death of Peter Sellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Life\_and\_Death\_of\_Peter\_Sellers "The Life and Death of Peter Sellers")_.

Theron played the eponymous rebel assassin in the science fiction action film _[Æon Flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%86on\_Flux\_(film) "Æon Flux (film)")_,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-9) and a miner fighting sexual harassment in the drama _[North Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_Country\_(film) "North Country (film)")_ (both in 2005).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-10) The latter role earned her a nomination for Best Actress at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-11) and the [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-12) In the same year, she voiced Æon Flux in the [tie-in video game adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%86on_Flux_(video_game) "Æon Flux (video game)") to the film for which she received the Best Performance by a Female award at the [Spike Video Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Video_Game_Awards "Spike Video Game Awards").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-13) Three years later, Theron starred in the superhero film _[Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock\_(film) "Hancock (film)")_ with [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith"). The film grossed over $624 million at the worldwide box office.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-14) She received a nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress– Motion Picture Comedy or Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Comedy_or_Musical "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Comedy or Musical") for her role as an alcoholic writer in the comedy-drama _[Young Adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Adult\_(film) "Young Adult (film)")_ (2011).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-16) The following year, Theron appeared in the action adventure film _[Snow White and the Huntsman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow\_White\_and\_the\_Huntsman "Snow White and the Huntsman")_ and [Ridley Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridley_Scott "Ridley Scott")'s science fiction film _[Prometheus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prometheus\_(2012\_film) "Prometheus (2012 film)")_. In 2015, she played [Imperator Furiosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperator_Furiosa "Imperator Furiosa") in [George Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Miller_(director) "George Miller (director)")'s _[Mad Max: Fury Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Max:\_Fury\_Road "Mad Max: Fury Road")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-17) Two years later, Theron appeared as criminal mastermind Cipher in the action film _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ (2017), a role she would reprise in _[F9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F9\_(film) "F9 (film)")_ (2021), _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_X "Fast X")_ (2023), and _[Fast Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_&\_Furious "Fast & Furious")_ (2028).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-18) Theron followed this with acclaimed performances in the comedy-drama _[Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tully\_(2018\_film) "Tully (2018 film)")_ (2018), the romantic comedy _[Long Shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Shot\_(2019\_film) "Long Shot (2019 film)")_ (2019), and the biographical drama _[Bombshell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombshell\_(2019\_film) "Bombshell (2019 film)")_ (2019), the lattermost of which earned her a third Academy Award nomination.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-19)

Performances by South African and American actress

[![Image 5: A headshot of Theron at the San Diego Comic-Con International in 2017.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/85/Charlize_Theron_in_2017.jpg/250px-Charlize_Theron_in_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Charlize_Theron_in_2017.jpg)

Theron at the 2017 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con")

Charlize Theron is a South African and American actress and producer who made her film debut in an uncredited role as a follower of a cult in the 1995 horror film _[Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children\_of\_the\_Corn\_III:\_Urban\_Harvest "Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-EW-2) Theron followed this with appearances as a hitman's girlfriend in _[2 Days in the Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2\_Days\_in\_the\_Valley "2 Days in the Valley")_,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-3) a waitress in the romantic comedy _[Trial and Error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial\_and\_Error\_(1997\_film) "Trial and Error (1997 film)")_ (1997),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-trial-4) and a woman plagued with demonic visions in the mystery thriller _[The Devil's Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Advocate\_(1997\_film) "The Devil's Advocate (1997 film)")_ (1997) with [Keanu Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keanu_Reeves "Keanu Reeves") and [Al Pacino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Pacino "Al Pacino").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-5) She appeared in the science fiction thriller _[The Astronaut's Wife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Astronaut's\_Wife "The Astronaut's Wife")_ with [Johnny Depp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Depp "Johnny Depp"), and [Lasse Hallström](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lasse_Hallstr%C3%B6m "Lasse Hallström")'s _[The Cider House Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cider\_House\_Rules "The Cider House Rules")_ (both in 1999). For her portrayal of serial killer [Aileen Wuornos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aileen_Wuornos "Aileen Wuornos") in the crime drama _[Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monster\_(2003\_film) "Monster (2003 film)")_ (2003), Theron received the [Academy Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-6) the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture– Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-7) and the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Female_Actor_in_a_Leading_Role "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Female Actor in a Leading Role").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-8) The following year, she played Swedish entertainer [Britt Ekland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britt_Ekland "Britt Ekland") in the biographical film _[The Life and Death of Peter Sellers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Life\_and\_Death\_of\_Peter\_Sellers "The Life and Death of Peter Sellers")_.

Theron played the eponymous rebel assassin in the science fiction action film _[Æon Flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%86on\_Flux\_(film) "Æon Flux (film)")_,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-9) and a miner fighting sexual harassment in the drama _[North Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_Country\_(film) "North Country (film)")_ (both in 2005).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-10) The latter role earned her a nomination for Best Actress at the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-11) and the [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-12) In the same year, she voiced Æon Flux in the [tie-in video game adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%86on_Flux_(video_game) "Æon Flux (video game)") to the film for which she received the Best Performance by a Female award at the [Spike Video Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Video_Game_Awards "Spike Video Game Awards").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-13) Three years later, Theron starred in the superhero film _[Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock\_(film) "Hancock (film)")_ with [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith"). The film grossed over $624 million at the worldwide box office.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-14) She received a nomination for the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress– Motion Picture Comedy or Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Comedy_or_Musical "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Motion Picture Comedy or Musical") for her role as an alcoholic writer in the comedy-drama _[Young Adult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Adult\_(film) "Young Adult (film)")_ (2011).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-16) The following year, Theron appeared in the action adventure film _[Snow White and the Huntsman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow\_White\_and\_the\_Huntsman "Snow White and the Huntsman")_ and [Ridley Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridley_Scott "Ridley Scott")'s science fiction film _[Prometheus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prometheus\_(2012\_film) "Prometheus (2012 film)")_. In 2015, she played [Imperator Furiosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperator_Furiosa "Imperator Furiosa") in [George Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Miller_(director) "George Miller (director)")'s _[Mad Max: Fury Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad\_Max:\_Fury\_Road "Mad Max: Fury Road")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-17) Two years later, Theron appeared as criminal mastermind Cipher in the action film _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fate\_of\_the\_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ (2017), a role she would reprise in _[F9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F9\_(film) "F9 (film)")_ (2021), _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_X "Fast X")_ (2023), and _[Fast Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_&\_Furious "Fast & Furious")_ (2028).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-18) Theron followed this with acclaimed performances in the comedy-drama _[Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tully\_(2018\_film) "Tully (2018 film)")_ (2018), the romantic comedy _[Long Shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long\_Shot\_(2019\_film) "Long Shot (2019 film)")_ (2019), and the biographical drama _[Bombshell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombshell\_(2019\_film) "Bombshell (2019 film)")_ (2019), the lattermost of which earned her a third Academy Award nomination.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlize_Theron_filmography#cite_note-19)

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.
