**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

### Jewish community

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-12)

## Geography

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

### Rail

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

### Jewish community

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-12)

## Geography

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

### Rail

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&printable=yes#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

### Jewish community

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

### Rail

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

### Jewish community

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

### Rail

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Jewish community

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Jewish community")]

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-12)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Transportation")]

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Rail")]

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benoni,_South_Africa#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

[[edit](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Road")]

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

### Jewish community

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-12)

## Geography

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

### Rail

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.

**Benoni** is a town on the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"), [Gauteng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauteng "Gauteng"), South Africa, some 26 kilometres (16 mi) east of [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg"), within the [City of Ekurhuleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Ekurhuleni_Metropolitan_Municipality "City of Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality") municipality.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-3)

Benoni was also the setting for the [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")-inspired movie _Crazy Monkey: Straight Outta Benoni_, released internationally in 2005.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-IMDB_tt0439518-4)

## History

### Jewish community

Benoni was previously home to a thriving [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") community, peaking with 400+ Jewish families. Jewish residents were also widely involved in the greater community, with five Jewish mayors- with the most famous being Morris Nestadt.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-5)

The Benoni Shul congregation began with a synagogue located on Woburn Avenue in 1907, before relocating to a new, larger synagogue on Park Street in 1933.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-6) The synagogue served the community for 90 years, before closing in 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-7) Rabbi Lionel Mirvis, father of [Chief Rabbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Rabbi "Chief Rabbi"), [Ephraim Mirvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ephraim_Mirvis "Ephraim Mirvis"), previously served the congregation.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-8) The synagogue was designed in a [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") style by the English architect, Arthur Furner, a partner in [Hermann Kallenbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kallenbach "Hermann Kallenbach")'s architectural firm, KKF.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-9)

The community was also served by Hillel, a Jewish day school, which closed in 1989, amid Jewish migration to Johannesburg's northern suburbs and emigration overseas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-10)

A Jewish cemetery was also established in Benoni in 1912, it is administered by the Benoni Chevrah Kadisha.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-11)

[Aura Herzog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_Herzog "Aura Herzog"), the former [First Lady of Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Israel "First Lady of Israel"), often spent [shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat") in Benoni when she was a student in [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-12)

## Geography

Benoni is situated towards the centre of the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand") and lies on the [urban fringe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Fringe "Urban Fringe") where the urban area dissolves into the smallholdings and farmland to the north. It borders on [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") to the north-west, [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") to the west, [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") to the south and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton") to the east.

Benoni mainly encompasses a mixture of suburban areas and semi-rural acreage towards the north while the commercial [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district") lies in the centre and a few industrial areas lie towards the south.

## Transportation

### Rail

Benoni lies on the main railway line between [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") and [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") and the main railway line between Johannesburg and [Daveyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daveyton "Daveyton"), both operated by [Metrorail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metrorail_Gauteng "Metrorail Gauteng") which has temporarily suspended services on these commuter lines since 2020 and have remained closed due to vandalism on these lines.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-14)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Springs line from Benoni to [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg_Park_station "Johannesburg Park station"), [Germiston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germiston "Germiston"), [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg"), [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and Springs. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Springs line including: Benoni station, New Kleinfontein station and Apex station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-:0-15)

Prior to 2020, Metrorail operated services on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line from Benoni to Johannesburg, Germiston and Boksburg. Benoni is served by three Metrorail railway stations on the Johannesburg-Daveyton line including: Avenue station, Northmead station and Van Ryn station.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benoni,_South_Africa&action=render#cite_note-:0-15)

### Road

The [N12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N12_(South_Africa) "N12 (South Africa)") is the major [freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeway "Freeway") that runs through Benoni. It enters the town from [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and [Johannesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannesburg "Johannesburg") in the west, bisecting the town and bypassing the CBD to its immediate north before heading east towards [eMalahleni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMalahleni "EMalahleni").

The [R23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R23_(South_Africa) "R23 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Kempton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton_Park,_South_Africa "Kempton Park, South Africa") towards [Brakpan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brakpan "Brakpan") and [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg,_Gauteng "Heidelberg, Gauteng") and runs through the CBD as Tom Jones Street (southbound) and Bunyan Street (northbound). The [R29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R29_(South_Africa) "R29 (South Africa)") runs east-west from [Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springs,_South_Africa "Springs, South Africa") towards [Boksburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boksburg "Boksburg") and runs through the CBD as Ampthill Avenue (westbound) and Princess Avenue (eastbound). The [R51](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R51_(South_Africa) "R51 (South Africa)") runs north-south from [Bapsfontein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapsfontein "Bapsfontein"), just outside Benoni towards Springs and barely by-passes Benoni to the east.

Benoni is also served by three [metropolitan routes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Routes_in_Johannesburg "Metropolitan Routes in Johannesburg") linking it to surrounding towns and cities in the [East Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rand "East Rand"). The [M43](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M43_(Johannesburg) "M43 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west and [Vosloorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vosloorus "Vosloorus") to the south-west. The [M44](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M44_(Johannesburg) "M44 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west. The [M45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M45_(Johannesburg) "M45 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Kempton Park to the north-west. The [M53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M53_(Johannesburg) "M53 (Johannesburg)") links Benoni with Boksburg to the west and Brakpan to the south.
